subproblem.title: The carrier is H^n-null inside a relatively compact open set on which the current vanishes
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set and W ⊆ ℝ^P. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be a GeometricCurrentOn U n, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) representing T: T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) = TestFormOn U n. Assume W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U, and T vanishes on W, i.e. T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Then H^n(M ∩ W) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ W) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–7 of the parent proof, for one fixed member W of the family 𝒲 (Simon 6.2.11 with 6.3.1 and 6.3.2(3); book/chapter-06.txt lines 296–303 and 763–768). Simon uses without proof that an integer multiplicity current carries no mass where it vanishes.
This proof uses the sibling unit_orientation_bounds: every ξ_0 ∈ Λ_n with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_0 Q satisfies ξ_0 ≠ 0 and ‖ξ_0‖ ≤ 1.
Notation.
- M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ, ξ := R.orient : ℝ^P → Λ_n.
- Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n and Λ_n := MultiVector P n = Λ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ, both with operator norms.
- H^n := μHE[n], C := closure W and ν := H^n⌞(M ∩ C) = μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C).
Fields of R used:
- M is measurable (measurableSet_carrier) and θ is measurable (measurable_mult).
- θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M (mult_pos).
- ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH^n ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (locallyIntegrable_mult).
- ξ is H^n⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
- For H^n⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q (orients).
Representation: T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Openness of U is not needed.
1. Measurability. M ∩ C is measurable because M is measurable and C is closed. W is measurable because it is open.
2. ν is finite and θ ∈ L¹(ν). C is compact and C ⊆ U, so locallyIntegrable_mult with K = C gives ∫⁻ θ dν = ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dH^n ≠ ∞. For x ∈ M ∩ C, θ(x) is a positive integer, so 1 ≤ θ(x). Hence
ν(ℝ^P) = H^n(M ∩ C) = ∫⁻_{M∩C} 1 dH^n ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dH^n < ∞ (setLIntegral_mono),
so ν is a finite measure. The real function x ↦ θ(x) is measurable and ∫⁻ θ dν < ∞, so it is ν-integrable (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top, using (θ(x) : [0,∞]).toReal = θ(x)).
3. Facts holding ν-a.e. Since M ∩ C ⊆ M, ν ≤ H^n⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono), so every H^n⌞M-a.e. property holds ν-a.e. (ae_mono).
- By orients and the sibling lemma, ξ(x) ≠ 0 and ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for H^n⌞M-a.e. x, hence for ν-a.e. x.
- ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure).
- ν-a.e. x lies in M ∩ C (ae_restrict_mem, using step 1).
4. Scalar components are integrable. Fix α ∈ Λ^n and put f_α(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α) ∈ ℝ.
- f_α is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: it is the product of the measurable θ with x ↦ ξ(x)(α), which is ξ composed with the continuous linear evaluation L ↦ L(α).
- For ν-a.e. x, ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm and step 3 give |f_α(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(α)| ≤ θ(x)·‖ξ(x)‖·‖α‖ ≤ ‖α‖·θ(x).
- Since ‖α‖·θ ∈ L¹(ν) by step 2, f_α ∈ L¹(ν) (Integrable.mono').
In particular f_α is locally integrable on W with respect to ν (Integrable.locallyIntegrable, then LocallyIntegrable.locallyIntegrableOn).
5. Testing T. Let α ∈ Λ^n, and let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W. Define ω(x) := g(x)·α.
- ω is C^∞ (g times a constant) and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
- tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ C ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left).
So ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W, and T(ω) = 0 because T vanishes on W. By the representation,
0 = T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)·α) dH^n(x).
If x ∈ M \ (M ∩ C), then x ∉ C ⊇ W, so x ∉ tsupport g and g(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). The integrand there is θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0. Since M is measurable and M ∩ C ⊆ M, the integral over M equals the integral over M ∩ C (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero, valid with or without integrability). By linearity of ξ(x), θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)·α) = g(x)·f_α(x). Hence
∫ g(x)·f_α(x) dν(x) = ∫_{M∩C} θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)·α) dH^n(x) = 0.
6. Fundamental lemma. ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel σ-algebra, and W is open. By step 4, f_α is locally integrable on W for ν. By step 5, ∫ g·f_α dν = 0 for every C^∞ g with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W. Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (real-valued case) then gives: for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ θ(x)·ξ(x)(α) = 0. For ν-a.e. x also x ∈ M (step 3), so θ(x) ≥ 1 > 0. Therefore, for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ ξ(x)(α) = 0.
7. Λ^n is finite-dimensional. Let e_1, …, e_P be the standard basis of ℝ^P. Define the linear map Φ : Λ^n → ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin P)} by Φ(α)(I) := α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}). Suppose Φ(α) = Φ(β). Then the underlying alternating maps of α and β agree on every tuple of basis vectors, so they are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating), and hence α = β (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). Thus Φ is an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space, so Λ^n is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective). Fix a basis α_1, …, α_N of Λ^n (Module.finBasis).
8. Conclusion. Apply step 6 to each α_k and intersect the finitely many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff): for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ ξ(x)(α_k) = 0 for all k. Take x in this set that also satisfies ξ(x) ≠ 0 (step 3); ν-a.e. x qualifies. If x ∈ W, the linear functional ξ(x) on Λ^n vanishes on a basis, so ξ(x) = 0 (Basis.ext for the underlying linear map, then ContinuousLinearMap.coe_injective). This contradicts ξ(x) ≠ 0. Hence ν-a.e. x satisfies x ∉ W, i.e. ν(W) = 0 (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem). As W is measurable, ν(W) = H^n(W ∩ (M ∩ C)) (Measure.restrict_apply). Since W ⊆ closure W = C, W ∩ (M ∩ C) = M ∩ W. Therefore H^n(M ∩ W) = 0.
proof_key_steps: ν := H^n⌞(M ∩ closure W) is a finite measure and θ ∈ L¹(ν), because closure W is a compact subset of U (locallyIntegrable_mult) and θ ≥ 1 on M.
By R.orients and unit_orientation_bounds, ξ ≠ 0 and ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 hold ν-a.e., so f_α = θ·ξ(α) is ν-integrable and |f_α| ≤ ‖α‖θ, for every covector α.
For g ∈ C_c^∞ with tsupport g ⊆ W, the form ω = g·α lies in TestFormOn U n with support in W, so 0 = T(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(gα) dH^n = ∫ g f_α dν.
The fundamental lemma on the open set W (IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero) gives ξ(α) = 0 ν-a.e. on W, since θ > 0 on M.
Λ^n is finite-dimensional (Basis.ext_alternating); testing a basis gives ξ = 0 ν-a.e. on W, contradicting ξ ≠ 0, so H^n(M ∩ W) = ν(W) = 0.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition includes every stated hypothesis, allows arbitrary U as the proof requires, and has a bare name with no competing DAG reservation. The proof establishes finite localization and scalar integrability, transfers orientation facts to the restricted measure, constructs admissible smooth test forms, justifies restriction of the integral, applies the fundamental lemma, cancels positive multiplicity, and uses a justified finite covector basis to obtain the contradiction. Its sole child dependency is correctly declared. The argument is complete, non-circular, and supplies precisely the local nullity needed for the selected parent's countable reduction.
